title: Electrospinning process window for antimicrobial polymer nanofibers
text: Electrospinning outcomes depend strongly on polymer concentration, applied voltage, flow rate, humidity, and collector distance. Lower polymer concentration can reduce fiber diameter, but too low a concentration causes beads and weak film formation. A moderate voltage window and low flow rate often improve jet stability. Cationic additives such as polyethyleneimine may improve antimicrobial surface activity, but cytocompatibility and leaching should be evaluated before application.

title: Design rules for PEI-modified nanofiber surfaces
text: Polyethyleneimine introduces amine-rich cationic surfaces that can increase interaction with microbial membranes. The same cationic character can increase cytotoxicity, so PEI fraction should be controlled. Surface modification after fiber formation may preserve morphology better than high bulk loading. A suitable next experiment should vary PEI fraction while keeping the base polymer and solvent system constant.

title: Surrogate modelling for polymer experiment planning
text: Small polymer datasets can support early-stage experiment planning when uncertainty is reported clearly. Random forests and Gaussian-process models are commonly used as surrogate models because they provide nonlinear response surfaces and practical uncertainty estimates. Expected improvement can rank candidate experiments, but recommendations must be validated by laboratory measurements.

title: RAG systems for scientific decision support
text: Retrieval-augmented generation is useful for scientific decision support when answers remain grounded in transparent evidence. A robust workflow should expose retrieved snippets, source identifiers, confidence or quality scores, and uncertainty flags. For high-stakes scientific claims, the system should avoid unsupported conclusions and recommend validation experiments.

title: Materials informatics workflow for lithium sulfur cathode screening
text: Lithium sulfur cathode performance is influenced by active material loading, conductive carbon fraction, binder chemistry, porosity, electrolyte amount, and cycling conditions. Informatics workflows can prioritize controlled comparisons before moving into complex multi-factor optimization. Candidate selection should include uncertainty estimates and clear experimental constraints.

title: Nanofiber morphology quality metrics
text: Nanofiber quality can be summarized by mean fiber diameter, diameter distribution, bead density, surface roughness, and coating uniformity. Automated image analysis can support reproducible morphology assessment, but segmentation and thresholding choices should be documented. Experimental planning should connect process variables to these measurable morphology metrics.
